HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Sabi wharf at dusk, autumn. Low two-shot from the wet planks. Councillor Sunchung in vermilion-red court robe, white hair, black cap with the gold flame, standing at the edge of the dock looking DOWN at a small black lacquer box being lifted from a boat — face tight, not proud. Beside him, a step closer to the boat: General Yunchung in grey steel lamellar with a cracked helm, red war-paint across both eyes, full black beard, grinning, one hand on the boat's gunwale as if the heads were a harvest. ONE device: the lacquer box as a dark rectangle between them. Low sun from the river raking their faces; gold #c9a24d on Sunchung's silk, ochre on Yunchung's plates. A dark out-of-focus rope in the foreground. Giwa warehouse eaves behind dissolving into dusk. EXACTLY two named people. New poses, never the portrait stance. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = seongchung, SECOND face = yunchung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_sabi_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). SUNCHUNG — Look: Elderly Baekje councillor: long white hair falling past the shoulders from under a small black silk cap with a single gold openwork flame-and-phoenix ornament pinned at the FRONT of the cap; full white beard and white moustache; heavy-lidded tired eyes, a deep crease between the brows, sun-weathered skin. Dress: Deep vermilion-red wide-sleeved court robe over a cream crossed inner collar, a dark indigo-blue sash, two carved jade toggles and a long red tassel hanging at the waist. Colour #c9a24d. YUNCHUNG — Look: Hard-bitten Baekje frontier general in his forties: full black beard, heavy scowling brows, a band of red war-paint smeared across both eyes, long black hair falling from under a dented round steel helm with a cracked crown and a short red-black plume knob. Dress: Grey steel lamellar with red-edged shoulder guards over an ochre-yellow robe, a broad red sash with a round bronze boss, red-and-black striped bracers; a ring-pommel sword in a red-lacquered scabbard. Colour #c9932a. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
